steps.name: Agree requirements and direction
steps.instructions: As the main agent, read project rules, the high-level project specification and the approved domain-organized OKF v0.2 requirements bundle inside docs/ (or the project's selected subdirectory). Include specifications prepared outside KOS. For a new project, first follow the client-side project-onboarding procedure and verify the real Git origin and publication route before creating this Brief; agreement to set up the repository is separate from agreement on Brief requirements. Discuss the problem, expected user outcome, boundaries, dependencies and testable acceptance criteria with the human in their language or the language specified by AGENTS.md. In all questions, progress updates and reports use plain, understandable language without unnecessary jargon or loanwords; give enough context to understand the decision and its consequence. Distinguish facts, assumptions and open questions. Explore proportionate normal, alternative, error and edge scenarios, including security-relevant cases. Number significant questions Q-01, Q-02, ... consecutively throughout this Brief (not anew per message or step); keep their answer, decision or unresolved status and rationale. In ordinary chat ask one question at a time and wait for its answer before the next. A question wizard may include several questions only if it presents them sequentially; otherwise use ordinary chat. When presenting a genuine choice, number its options 1., 2., ... and ask for a reply with one digit for that question; option numbers are separate from Q IDs. Recommend an option with a short reason in parentheses; for free-form questions suggest a useful approach with a short reason, without inventing factual answers. Compare realistic high-level options when there is a genuine choice; record accepted and rejected approaches with reasons, not invented alternatives. Present the proposed required behavior, criteria, decisions, remaining questions and high-level delivery direction for separate explicit human approval after the questions have been answered. Do not decide product ambiguities on the human's behalf; consequential unresolved questions keep this step open. Technical implementation details permitted by project rules may be left to Execution. Before explicit agreement on Brief requirements, do not write KOS artifacts, create dependent tasks/groups or edit the normative project specification. If agreement cannot be reliably recovered, ask again. Do not advance without it.

steps.name: Record specification and decompose
steps.instructions: As the main agent, verify explicit human agreement against project rules and existing high-level and domain specifications; resolve contradictory or lost decisions with the human before writing. Save approved high-level requirements, normative specification and implementation_plan in KOS. Keep the consecutive Brief Q numbers across the discussion and documents, with answers or explicit open status. For significant work use stable project/task-qualified REQ, AC and DEC IDs; link requirements, criteria, decisions with alternatives and rationale, questions and tasks, without tagging every code line. Record nonblocking questions with an owner and point of resolution; never silently convert an open product question into an approved requirement. Create at least one planned task using KOS Execution v2; create an epic group if needed. Create each dependent task atomically with blocked_by_ids including this Brief and other required blockers. Specify task outcome, boundaries, relevant criterion IDs and path to the normative specification. Inspect created IDs and dependencies; save planning_report with criterion-to-task coverage, gaps and relationships. Explicitly load kos-project-docs and prepare the approved normative OKF v0.2 concept in the verified project worktree within docs/ or the project's selected subdirectory, under the appropriate business domain or game aspect; maintain navigation. Describe what should hold independently of implementation progress. Review the draft and run applicable document checks. Reconcile partial failures against existing artifacts, files and tasks without duplicates; do not advance until results are complete.

templates.requirements:
# Approved requirements

## Problem, user outcome and boundaries
<Who needs what; what is excluded; relevant dependencies.>

## Requirements and acceptance criteria
<List stable project/task-qualified REQ and AC IDs; describe testable normal, alternative, error, edge and security-relevant behavior.>

## Decisions and questions
<List DEC IDs with accepted/rejected options and rationale; retain consecutive Q IDs with answers or explicit open status, owner and resolution point. Distinguish assumptions from approved facts.>

## Approval
<Record what was explicitly agreed with the human and when; do not infer consent from a mode switch.>
templates.specification:
# Approved required behavior

## Scope and normative source
<Link requirements, applicable project specifications and the maintained project Markdown file; distinguish this approved snapshot from implementation progress.>

## User scenarios
<For each relevant REQ/AC ID, describe expected normal, alternative, error and edge outcomes and limits, including security-relevant cases.>

## Decisions and unresolved questions
<Reference DEC and consecutive Q IDs; give rationale, owner and resolution point for nonblocking open questions. Do not present an open decision as approved.>

## Acceptance
<State observable criteria and links to their originating requirements.>
templates.implementation_plan:
# High-level delivery plan

## Approach and dependencies
<Describe direction, boundaries, ordering and major risks, not a finished task-level design. Reference approved REQ/AC/DEC IDs.>

## Proposed work packages
<Map each planned outcome to criteria and required dependencies; concrete implementation is refined in each Execution task.>

## Decisions and open questions
<Retain consecutive Brief Q IDs with answers or explicit status, owner and resolution point; do not assume unresolved behavior is approved.>

## Verification and publication direction
<How criteria will be checked; where the normative document is to be published.>
templates.planning_report:
# Decomposition and coverage

## Created tasks and group
<List verified task IDs, outcome, boundaries, group if any, workflow ID and blocked_by IDs, including this Brief.>

## Criterion-to-task coverage
<Map each approved AC ID to at least one created task ID and intended verification; state gaps or overlapping ownership explicitly.>

## Normative specification
<Give the maintained project document path and relevant approved REQ/DEC/Q references.>

## Reconciliation
<Identify existing versus newly created records after retries; record unresolved gaps without inventing duplicates.>

steps.name: Publish and verify specification
steps.instructions: As the main agent, check the approved normative project file, links, KOS artifacts, criterion-to-task coverage and blocked dependencies. Inspect status, complete diff and project publication rules; run applicable checks and review the final changes. Publish the specification at the project-defined destination and independently verify the published revision there before completing Brief and unblocking its tasks. On prohibition or undefined destination seek a human decision; on ambiguous outcome inspect the destination before retrying. Preserve the worktree and do not create duplicate tasks. Save publication_report with document path, destination and verifiable revision/link; reconcile planning_report if needed. Only then complete Brief under the active claim.

templates.publication_report:
# Brief specification publication

## Published document
<Approved project file path, destination, verifiable revision or link and observed result at that destination.>

## Pre-publication checks
<Final diff, links, document checks, approved criteria and task/dependency coverage; include actual outcomes.>

## Completion evidence
<Confirm that the published specification was verified before completing Brief; note any remaining gaps or conflicts. Do not claim success on ambiguous publication.>
